subject: if_else and if use in stan

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: if_else and if use in stan
parts:
Hi,

It appears that the statements
        if (i == 1) {
            c <- 0;
        } else {
            c <- B [i - 1];
        }
and
c <- if_else (i == 1, 0, B [i - 1]); are not equivalent since out of bounds error is thrown for each i==1.

It would be great to be able to use the short form because it makes code more readable.

Thank you,
Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] if_else and if use in stan
parts:
I'd rather not change the behavior of if_else(), which is a function.
Functions always evaluate all their arguments in Stan (and in C++).

As an alternative, I propose actually implementing the conditional
operator (cond ? a : b) with short-circuiting.

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1125

As of Stan 2.5, I fixed the operators || and && so they short circuit.
But that's all that short circuites (other than if/then statements, of course).

- Bob
